scope: full claim inventory: 411 items (222 draft sentences and fragments, 87 data/README.md, 33 docs/sources.json entries, 32 [allow] reasons, 17 README.md, 12 [published] sentences, 4 [claims] licences, 4 charts)
method: Each lens refuted its primary items and any others it chose; every non-confirmed verdict was re-checked by an independent skeptic (two skeptics were re-run after the host slept; the ten completed agents replayed from cache). A finding stands only if the skeptic upheld it; ten the skeptics did not uphold were re-executed by the adjudicator and struck with evidence. The adjudicator added one finding ([226]) and resolved the two UNVERIFIABLE reference years with Internet Archive captures.

findings.claim: # Forced to Save, and I Never Knew It
findings.evidence: adjudicator: Title holds as legal compulsion (PP 46/2015 Pasal 2(2): every working person must register in JHT) plus the owner's own account (gate.toml [claims]); the unverified deposit is handled at [7], [84] and [329]. | H: The title stands on the owner's account. gate.toml [claims] licenses it with 'was not aware of the BPJS Ketenagakerjaan JHT deduction', and design A4 (docs/2026-10-21-jht-401k-design.md:129) records it as the owner's choice. Nothing on file shows that contributions were actually made for him: he chose not to check JMO. BPJS's own 2022 report lists employer non-compliance among its obstacles: 'Masih adanya Pemberi Kerja/Badan Usaha yang belum patuh untuk memberikan perlindungan jaminan sosial ketenagakerjaan kepada para pekerja' (sources/text/bpjs_ir_2022.txt:14254-14262, PDF p.88). Active JHT wage earners at end-2024 (18,425,867, sources.json bpjs_ir2024_jht_active) were 28.3% of ILO-modelled employees in 2024 (65,033.154 thousand, data/ilo_idn_employment_by_status.csv). Audit item 10 calls that ratio a rough measure. Read as a statement of legal compulsion, the title holds. | skeptic H: The title rests on the owner's account, and that account is the agreed basis for any personal sentence. gate.toml:54 records his words as 'was not aware of the BPJS Ketenagakerjaan JHT deduction'. Read naturally, 'the deduction' assumes there was one on his pay. Design A4 (docs/2026-10-21-jht-401k-design.md:129-131) records that he chose the title as 'true by his own account'. 'Forced' in the legal sense is backed by PP 46/2015 Pasal 2(1) and 2(2) (pp_46_2015.txt:118-125). All of the round-1 evidence is about the whole population, and I re-ran it: the BPJS 2022 obstacle that some employers are 'belum patuh' (bpjs_ir_2022.txt:1344-1347 and 14255-14260), and 18,425,867 / 65,033,154 = 0.2833 (sources.json bpjs_ir2024_jht_active against the 2024 'Employees' row of data/ilo_idn_employment_by_status.csv, 65033.154 thousand). None of it can tell us about one worker whose own account assumes the deduction. The finding itself concludes that the title holds and proposes no change. Its line 'he chose not to check JMO' is not on file: I grepped docs/, gate.toml and README.md and found nothing.

findings.claim: Part of the pay goes into it before you can spend it, it lowers your taxable income, and the employer adds money of its own.
findings.evidence: H: These are the owner's own three reasons. Note: a US economist can still cite Roth deferrals and plans with no employer money. 'can lower' or 'often adds' would close that gap.

findings.claim: I worked on a payroll in Indonesia, and under Indonesian law a share of that pay went into an old-age savings account: Jaminan Hari Tua, or JHT, run by BPJS Ketenagakerjaan.
findings.evidence: H: 'I worked on a payroll in Indonesia' is an owner fact. 'under Indonesian law a share of that pay went into' states as fact that contributions were made, which the owner has not checked (no JMO check, no payslip). The law puts the duty on the employer 'sesuai penahapan kepesertaan' (pp_46_2015.txt:118-121). BPJS's 2022 report names employer non-compliance as an obstacle (bpjs_ir_2022.txt:1342-1346 and 14254-14262). By a rough measure, active JHT wage earners were 28.3% of ILO-modelled employees in 2024 (computed from sources.json bpjs_ir2024_jht_active and data/ilo_idn_employment_by_status.csv). Coverage is far from universal, so the law alone does not establish his deduction. | skeptic H: The finding's evidence checks out, but it answers a different question. Pasal 2(1) does say 'sesuai penahapan kepesertaan' (pp_46_2015.txt:118-121), BPJS does name non-compliant employers as an obstacle (bpjs_ir_2022.txt:1344-1347, 14255-14260), and the ratio is 28.3%. That shows the law alone does not prove his deduction. The sentence, though, rests on the owner's account, not on the law alone: he was 'not aware of the BPJS Ketenagakerjaan JHT deduction' (gate.toml:54), which assumes a deduction from his pay, and A4 records 'Forced to Save' as true by his own account. Coverage across the population cannot overturn one person's account. The proposed 'should have gone into' would contradict the title the owner chose (A4).
findings.fix: Narrowed 'went into' to 'should have gone into': the owner was not aware of the deduction and has not checked a payslip or JMO; to be confirmed by the owner at the checkpoint.

findings.claim: It works by letting you watch your money grow.
findings.evidence: L: The thesis 'It works by letting you watch your money grow' is labelled 'My answer, before any data' and is never tested. The growth test models balances, not what savers see. The post's only evidence on how the 401(k) gets people saving is [59]-[60]: 'does not leave saving to chance', with automatic enrollment in 61% of plans and 85% participation. That points to a default mechanism. No sentence claims the data proves the thesis, but 'What Indonesia can learn' ([77]-[83]) builds only on the untested visibility mechanism and never reconciles it with [59]. | skeptic L: The design doc section 1 records this as the owner's stance, and the post labels it 'before any data', so it is licensed as opinion. But nothing in the analysis tests it: build_analysis computes modelled real balances, not what savers see or why they save. The post's only mechanism evidence, [59]-[60] (line 54), is automatic enrollment in 61% of Vanguard plans, a default. 'What Indonesia can learn' builds on the visibility mechanism without reconciling it with [59]. The claim is unverifiable from the post's data as the finding says. | C: The thesis 'It works by letting you watch your money grow' is labelled the owner's prior 'before any data', and no result in the post tests that mechanism. The post's own Vanguard source points to a different mechanism. HAS 2026 p.6 (2024): voluntary-enrollment participant-weighted participation is 64%, against 94% under automatic enrollment, and 61% of plans auto-enroll. A hostile reader can set these figures against the thesis: participation is driven largely by default enrollment, not by savers watching growth. Item 59 partly acknowledges this ('does not leave saving to chance'). | skeptic C: The sentence is framed as the owner's prior: draft line 7 opens 'My answer, before any data'. The design doc (docs/2026-10-21-jht-401k-design.md:8, under '1. Question and stance (the owner's)') records 'The 401(k) is not compulsory, yet it works because savers watch their money grow.' No result in results.json tests this mechanism; growth, contributions and what BPJS publishes are all measured, but whether watching causes saving is not. The HAS figures the finding cites check out (vanguard_how_america_saves_2026.txt:192,204,206, 2024 column): 61% of plans auto-enroll, and participant-weighted participation is 64% under voluntary enrollment against 94% under automatic enrollment. The post's own data therefore point to defaults as a major driver, and draft line 54 partly concedes this. One more point for the owner: the stance is in the design doc but is not among the owner-supplied personal facts this round lists, so the owner should confirm the wording is his. | H: Framed as the owner's pre-data answer (design §1), and the post never says it tested this mechanism. Note for the owner: a US economist can quote the post's own source against it. HAS p.11 (txt:469-473) says employees in automatic-enrollment plans 'saved an average of 12.2%' against 7.5% in voluntary plans, which puts much of the 401(k)'s effect in defaults; [59]-[60] concede the same point. Any surface that repeats this claim should keep the 'before any data' frame.
findings.fix: Kept as the owner's labelled pre-data answer ('My answer, before any data'); no sentence claims the data confirm it, and the sentence that used it as a mechanism ([83]) is narrowed to 'could'. findings.claim: JHT is compulsory for wage earners.
findings.evidence: S: 'JHT is compulsory for wage earners' is an uncited universal. PP 46 Pasal 2(1), p.3, makes registration compulsory only for 'Pemberi Kerja selain penyelenggara negara ... sesuai penahapan kepesertaan', i.e. by stages. Pasal 3 leaves state employers to a separate regulation, and Pasal 4(1)(a) limits wage-earner members to non-state employers. The post's own source IR 2024 p.92 shows active wage earners at 29,308,491 in JKK/JKM against only 18,425,867 in JHT: about 10.9 million wage earners covered by BPJS are not in JHT. [7] ('under Indonesian law a share of that pay went into...') and [84] rest on this universal; the owner did not check JMO. | skeptic S: The universal carries no citation. sources/text/pp_46_2015.txt (Pasal 2(1)) puts the duty on 'Setiap Pemberi Kerja selain penyelenggara negara ... sesuai penahapan kepesertaan', so it applies to employers other than the state, and in stages. Pasal 3 leaves workers of state employers to a separate regulation. Pasal 4(1)(a) defines wage-earner participants as those at non-state employers. sources/text/bpjs_ir_2024.txt lines 8427-8437: 29,308,491 active wage-earner (PU) members in JKK/JKM against 18,425,867 PU members in JHT. That leaves about 10.9 million BPJS-covered wage earners outside JHT. The refuter's narrowing, 'at private employers', brings in a new error: the law's group is employers other than the state, which includes state-owned enterprises, not just private firms. | L: 'JHT is compulsory for wage earners' (and [76] 'the money goes in by law', [7] 'under Indonesian law a share of that pay went into'). PP 46/2015 Pasal 2 ayat (1), pp_46_2015.txt lines 116-119, obliges employers to register workers in JHT 'sesuai penahapan kepesertaan' (according to phased membership). The stored IR 2024 (bpjs_ir_2024.txt lines 8425-8436) counts 29,308,491 active wage-earner (PU) participants but only 18,425,867 PU participants in JHT. Being on a payroll does not by law or in practice put a worker in JHT, so the post's 'hard part' premise and the owner's 'went into' rest on his employer having been phased in. The owner did not check JMO. | skeptic L: sources/text/pp_46_2015.txt lines 116-121, Pasal 2 ayat (1): employers must register themselves and their workers in JHT 'sesuai penahapan kepesertaan'; the elucidation (lines 1021-1027) defines this as phasing under the social security phasing regulations. sources/text/bpjs_ir_2024.txt lines 8425-8436: 29.308.491 active PU participants in JKK and JKM but only 18.425.867 PU in JHT, so about 10.9 million active wage-earner participants are not in JHT. No sources.json key licenses 'compulsory'. The excerpt in gate.toml ('Indonesia already makes wage earners save through JHT') repeats the universal. The [7] part of the finding over-reaches: the owner's account (gate.toml claims line 54) is that he 'was not aware of the BPJS Ketenagakerjaan JHT deduction', which presupposes the deduction was taken, so 'went into' rests on his own fact; [76] 'the money goes in by law' is true for enrolled members under Pasal 16. | H: PP 46/2015 Pasal 2(1) obliges only 'Pemberi Kerja selain penyelenggara negara' to register their workers, 'sesuai penahapan kepesertaan' (pp_46_2015.txt:118-121). Pasal 3 leaves workers of state employers to a separate regulation (txt:130-133). Pasal 4(1)(a) limits wage-earner participants to non-state employers (txt:140-142). A civil-servant reader is a wage earner but is not in JHT. | skeptic H: The finding misreads the stored text. Pasal 3 (pp_46_2015.txt:131-134) does not exclude workers at state employers from JHT. It says 'Penyelenggaraan program JHT bagi Peserta pada Pemberi Kerja penyelenggara negara diatur dalam Peraturan Pemerintah tersendiri': JHT for participants at state employers is run under a separate regulation, which treats them as JHT participants. Pasal 2(2) (txt:122-125) makes registration a duty for 'Setiap orang yang bekerja ... sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan'. Pasal 4(1)(a) limits who is covered by this regulation, not who is covered by JHT. The stored files therefore do not show that 'a civil-servant reader ... is not in JHT'. One gap remains: the duty applies 'sesuai penahapan kepesertaan' (txt:121), and no stored file says who that phasing leaves out.
findings.fix: Deleted: PP 46/2015 Pasal 2(1) phases employers in and Pasal 3 and 4 leave state employers out; IR 2024 p.92 counts 29,308,491 active wage-earner members in JKK/JKM against 18,425,867 in JHT.

findings.claim: Each month 5.7 percent of wages goes in: 2 percent from the worker and 3.7 percent from the employer (Pemerintah Republik Indonesia, 2015b).
findings.evidence: S: PP 46/2015 Pasal 16(1), sources/text/pp_46_2015.txt p.11 (sha ok, quote occurs once): 'Iuran JHT bagi Peserta penerima Upah yang bekerja pada Pemberi Kerja selain penyelenggara negara sebesar 5,7% ... a. 2% ... ditanggung oleh Pekerja; dan b. 3,7% ... ditanggung oleh Pemberi Kerja'. Pasal 17 sets the base as 'Upah sebulan'. Bound keys pp46_jht_contribution.values.total_pct/worker_pct/employer_pct are the right ones. The scope (non-state employers) is the issue raised on [18] in extras. | H: sources.json pp46_jht_contribution quote gives 5,7% / 2% / 3,7%, and the bound keys are correct. The quote applies to 'Pemberi Kerja selain penyelenggara negara'; the fix to [18] covers that scope.

findings.claim: A separate pension scheme, Jaminan Pensiun, takes another 3 percent (Pemerintah Republik Indonesia, 2015a); it pays a pension rather than building a balance, so I leave it out of the growth comparison.
findings.evidence: S: The 3% is right: PP 45/2015 Pasal 28(2), pp_45_2015.txt p.20. But the stored PP 45 contradicts 'rather than building a balance'. Pasal 24(1) gives a member who reaches pension age with under 15 years of contributions 'seluruh akumulasi Iurannya ditambah hasil pengembangannya', and Pasal 3(4)(b) ends membership on receiving 'akumulasi Iuran beserta hasil pengembangannya secara sekaligus'. The 3% also applies only up to a wage ceiling (Pasal 29(2): Rp7,000,000 in 2015, indexed), and IR 2024 p.92 counts 14,959,033 JP members against 18,425,867 wage-earner JHT members, so not every JHT payer pays JP. DB status is supported ('Program Jaminan Pensiun merupakan program manfaat pasti', elucidation). | skeptic S: The 3% is right: sources/text/pp_45_2015.txt lines 820-829 (Pasal 28(2), '3% (tiga persen) dari Upah per bulan'). Defined-benefit status is also right: line 1085-1088 of the elucidation ('Program Jaminan Pensiun merupakan program manfaat pasti'). But the same regulation also builds an accumulation. Pasal 24(1) (lines 737-742): a member who reaches pension age with under 15 years of contributions 'berhak mendapatkan seluruh akumulasi Iurannya ditambah hasil pengembangannya'. Pasal 24(3) adds that the returns are 'dihitung setiap bulan berdasarkan nilai sebenarnya'. Pasal 3(4)(b) (lines 170-175) ends membership on receiving 'akumulasi Iuran beserta hasil pengembangannya secara sekaligus'. So 'rather than building a balance' is false for that group of members. The wage ceiling (Pasal 29(2), line 857, Rp7,000,000 in 2015) is real, but the sentence makes no claim about it, so it needs no change. | H: sources.json pp45_jp_total gives 3%. Note: under PP 45/2015 (pp_45_2015.txt:739-742), a member who reaches pension age with fewer than 15 years of contributions gets 'seluruh akumulasi Iurannya ditambah hasil pengembangannya' as a lump sum. 'pays a pension rather than building a balance' describes the main benefit fairly, and the reason for excluding JP holds.
findings.fix: Deleted 'rather than building a balance' (PP 45/2015 Pasal 24(1) pays accumulated contributions plus returns to members with under 15 years).

findings.claim: The money is not locked up the way a 401(k) is.
findings.evidence: H: The post's own 401(k) source contradicts 'locked up'. In 2024, 94% of plans in How America Saves offered hardship withdrawals and 80% offered loans (vanguard_how_america_saves_2026.txt:304, 312; Highlights p.8). The contrast the next two sentences actually show is a 10% additional tax on early withdrawal, which is a cost, not a lock. JHT also allows a partial withdrawal while still working (pp_46_2015.txt:590-602, Pasal 22(4)-(6)). A US economist can quote this sentence against the post. | skeptic H: Confirmed. In the 2024 column of How America Saves, 80% of plans offered loans (vanguard_how_america_saves_2026.txt:304) and 94% offered hardship withdrawals (txt:312). While still working, JHT is the more locked of the two: Pasal 22(4)-(6) (pp_46_2015.txt:590-602) allows one partial withdrawal, only after 10 years of membership, capped at 30% for housing or 10% for other uses. The real contrast comes when a worker leaves a job: a one-month wait for JHT ([22]) against a 10% additional tax for a 401(k) ([23]). That tax is a cost, not a lock. As a general statement, [21] misleads, and [22] and [23] make the precise contrast without it.
findings.fix: Deleted (HAS 2026: 94% of plans offer hardship withdrawals, 80% loans; JHT allows a partial withdrawal while working, PP 46 Pasal 22(4)-(6)).

findings.claim: A worker who resigns can take the JHT balance in cash after a waiting period of one month (Menteri Ketenagakerjaan, 2022; Pemerintah Republik Indonesia, 2015c).

findings.claim: [[published] seoTitle] Forced to Save, and I Never Knew It - Jonathan Chrisnaldy
findings.evidence: H: Matches the title. The separator is a hyphen, not a dash. The verdict on [1] applies.

findings.claim: [[published] excerpt] The US 401(k) is voluntary, yet its savers watch their money grow.
findings.evidence: H: Read as description it is supported: statements are furnished automatically each quarter (dol_fab_2006-03.txt:28-30), and 80% of participants were registered for website access in 2024 (vanguard_how_america_saves_2026.txt:329). Note: it drops the body's 'my answer, before any data' frame, and 'yet' suggests a causal story that HAS p.11 (12.2% saved in automatic-enrollment plans against 7.5% in voluntary ones) complicates. 'can watch' would be safer.

findings.claim: [[published] excerpt] Indonesia already makes wage earners save through JHT, and I paid in without knowing.
findings.evidence: H: 'I paid in without knowing' states his contributions as fact; they are unverified, as in [7]. 'makes wage earners save' turns a legal duty into an outcome, against BPJS's own non-compliance obstacle (bpjs_ir_2022.txt:14254-14262) and roughly 28% coverage. The excerpt is shown on its own in search results and on cards, with no body text to qualify it. | skeptic H: This stands for the first clause only. 'Makes wage earners save' uses causative 'make', which says the saving happens. As a general statement, BPJS's own obstacle of employers that are 'belum patuh' contradicts that (bpjs_ir_2022.txt:1344-1347, 14255-14260), and the excerpt is shown on its own with no qualifying text (gate.toml:68). The second clause, 'I paid in without knowing', rests on the owner's account, as in items 1, 7 and 84 (gate.toml:54; A4). The round-1 change to 'I did not know it existed' is not needed. 'Wage earners' is not too broad either: see item 18 (Pasal 2(2) and Pasal 3).
findings.fix: Narrowed to 'Indonesia already requires workers to save through JHT, and I did not know it existed.' ('I paid in' is unverified; 'makes ... save' read as an outcome).

findings.claim: [[published] excerpt] From 2005 to 2020, the same yearly saving became 1.4 times what was put in at JHT's rate, after Indonesian inflation, and 2.4 times in an S&P 500 fund, after US inflation.
findings.evidence: adjudicator: Judgement call, kept: results.json jht 1.3798 and sp500 2.4127 print as 1.4 and 2.4, each with its own inflation tag; the body states the risk ([44]-[46]). Offered to the owner as an option at the checkpoint. | H: 'the same yearly saving became 1.4 times ... at JHT's rate ... and 2.4 times in an S&P 500 fund' reads as a choice between two homes for one saving, which the body explicitly disavows ([46]). It carries no risk caveat: the S&P line fell to 0.73 in 2008 while JHT stood at 1.02 (results.json growth.sp500.low, growth.jht.path.2008). Its only qualifiers are the two inflation tags. An Indonesian reader can take it as '2.4 if I had chosen differently'. | skeptic H: Both numbers reproduce: results.json growth.jht.multiple 1.3798 rounds to 1.4, and growth.sp500.multiple 2.4127 rounds to 2.4. 'The same yearly saving' matches how the body itself sets up the test ([30] 'The test follows a single saver', [33] 'I run it four ways'). Each figure carries its own inflation tag. Leaving out the risk caveat is an editorial choice for a summary, not a claim that is wrong, unsupported or unverifiable. Nothing in the excerpt tells anyone what to choose. A REFUTED verdict goes too far.

The second clause, on the unpublished rate, is supported (see [331]). | skeptic H: Confirmed for the first clause. 'Requires' is supported by PP 46/2015 Pasal 2(1)-(2) (pp_46_2015.txt:118-125). The second clause holds: results.json published.last_credited_year = 2020, and years_without_credited = 2021 to 2025.

findings.claim: [[published] alt:jh-3-contributions.png] Bar chart of what goes in each year as a share of pay, worker and employer: Singapore's CPF, 37 percent for workers aged 55 and under; a 401(k) in plans Vanguard keeps records for, 12.1 percent on average in 2024; JHT, 5.7 percent; JP, a separate pension, 3 percent.
findings.evidence: C: The published alt text for chart 3 says '37 percent for workers aged 55 and under' without the top-wage-band scope. The dataset description says the rates apply to the highest wage band (wages of $750 or more per month); same issue as item 58. | skeptic C: Alt text describes the image, and this one does so accurately: the rendered chart's bar reads 'CPF, Singapore (aged 55 and under)' with the label '37% of pay', and it shows no band. The wage-band scope is not missing from the published figure. The figcaption inside the same <figure> element (site MDX lines 80-84, line 83) says 'CPF Board contribution rates in force on 1 January 2026 for wages in the top band', and screen readers read it together with the image. The alt text adds no claim beyond what the chart and its caption show, so omitting the footnote caveat is a style or accessibility preference, not a factual error. Item 58 differs: it is the author's freestanding prose claim. | H: 12.1% is the 'average total participant contribution rate'. HAS p.45 says 'These rates exclude eligible nonparticipants', and here it stands beside JHT's statutory 5.7% for every covered worker (audit item 7). Read alone, 'on average' suggests every eligible worker. | skeptic H: The alt text describes the chart bar '401(k), Vanguard plans (2024)' (make_charts.py:151). '12.1 percent on average' for 'a 401(k)' is the average total going into 401(k) accounts that receive contributions. The reading 'every eligible worker' only arises if 'worker' replaces 'a 401(k)', and the alt text does not say 'worker'. Item 56 does say 'worker', which is why it fails and this does not. Body [55] calls it 'a typical 401(k) saver'.
